primary_cause: Evidence supports stronger Capesize demand and elevated dry-bulk rates during 2026, but counter evidence indicates the strength may be substantially driven by temporary rerouting and could reverse into a 2027 supply glut. The persistence and exact breadth of the current commodity-volume freight cycle remain unresolved.
counter_evidence: BIMCO warned that apparent 2026 dry-bulk strength was substantially artificial because of forced rerouting and could reverse into a 2027 supply glut. [Dry bulk shipping faces 2027 supply glut: BIMCO warns Hormuz rerouting boost will reverse] https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/other/dry-bulk-shipping-faces-2027-supply-glut-bimco-warns-hormuz-rerouting-boost-will-reverse/ar-AA29coQf
source_summary: A key dry-bulk rate measure reached its highest level since December 2023, driven by rising Capesize demand and tightening vessel supply. [Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand] https://gcaptain.com/dry-bulk-shipping-rates-hit-two-year-high-on-capesize-demand/

primary_cause: Available evidence points to structural storage demand and supply constraints, but it does not establish a current, time-consistent NAND pricing, SSD/controller/module demand, or inventory cycle. Industry evidence also describes continued growth rather than a clearly defined cyclical upswing.
counter_evidence: The 2026 Future of Memory and Storage Conference reported continued growth in the storage and memory market, without evidence of a weakening NAND cycle. [2026 FMS Shows Storage And Memory Market Continued Growth] https://www.forbes.com/sites/tomcoughlin/2026/08/16/2026-fms-shows-storage-and-memory-market-continued-growth/
source_summary: The NAND market is described as entering a period in which supply may not catch demand as it did in prior cycles.
